lines.text: A candle flame looks like it burns the wick. It does not.
lines.visual: Engraved candle on ink; the flame glows; a leader names the wick, then a stamp says NOT THE WICK.

lines.text: The heat melts the wax, the wick draws the liquid up, and the flame burns wax vapour, a few millimetres above the wick.
lines.visual: Camera pushes in: a melt pool, an arrow up the wick, and a hatched vapour zone just above it.

lines.text: Each gram of wax meets oxygen from the air and leaves as two invisible gases: carbon dioxide and water vapour.
lines.visual: Bone paper: WAX + OXYGEN, arrows to two gases, all inside the Shorts square.

lines.text: So the candle does not vanish. It turns into air you cannot see.
lines.visual: The two gases rise and fade; one serif line closes the plate.
